=== meeting_notes ===
Planning meeting with James and Caroline Whitmore, held 20 May 2026. This was a long meeting covering the recent sale of James's business and what to do with the proceeds.
By way of background: James completed the sale of his company in April. It has been a busy and slightly emotional period for them both, having built the business over many years.
The headline structure of the deal: a completion payment of £850,000 was received on completion and is currently sitting in a solicitor's client account ready to be moved.
On top of the completion payment, the deal includes a deferred earnout of up to £400,000, payable over the next two years and contingent on the business hitting agreed revenue targets. None of the earnout has been received yet, and James was clear it is not guaranteed; it depends entirely on how the business performs under the new owners.
Important point on the completion money: £200,000 of the £850,000 is already committed to repaying a bridging loan James took out last year against the business. That repayment is due shortly.
James and Caroline's objectives are long-term growth with a balanced-to-moderate risk appetite. They have no income requirement from the portfolio currently; James may do some consultancy work but nothing is settled.
Their overriding objective for this money is clear: to build a tax-efficient base that can replace James's income when he steps back from full-time work in about three years. We agreed everything we recommend should be weighed against that three-year goal.
They mentioned they would like, at some stage, to help with school fees for their grandchildren and possibly make a charitable donation. Both were clear these are aspirations for the future and nothing should be actioned on them in this report.
We then went through the existing portfolio, which is spread across three platforms. I had the latest snapshot in front of me but we cross-checked some of it live.
On the Holloway platform they each hold a Stocks & Shares ISA, and there is a jointly-held General Investment Account. The joint GIA is the one that has moved most: pulling it up live, it was showing around £255,000. That is noticeably higher than the figure on the snapshot I had, which was struck back in February before the spring run-up.
On the Brightwell platform James holds a SIPP and Caroline holds a SIPP. There is also a second jointly-held General Investment Account on Brightwell. These were all in line with the snapshot and we did not see any need to revise them.
On the Meridian platform there is a jointly-held offshore investment bond, and James holds a cash account there. Caroline also has a cash account on Meridian, but she could not remember the balance and thought it might be fairly small; she will confirm it for us.
Caroline also mentioned an old Meridian account in her name that was closed last year; that one has nothing in it and can be disregarded. I noted it only so we do not chase a balance that does not exist.
On the plan for the available proceeds: we agreed to use both ISA allowances for the new tax year, make pension contributions into both SIPPs up to the appropriate level, add to the Holloway joint GIA, and place the remaining balance into a new jointly-held investment account.
As part of tidying up, we agreed to disinvest a portion of the Holloway joint GIA and rebalance it; that sale is a disposal and will have a capital gains position to set out.
Caroline asked about the total ongoing cost of all this across the three platforms. I said I would set out the charges in the report once I had verified each platform's figures rather than estimate them in the meeting.
We also briefly discussed the offshore bond and whether it still suited them; we agreed to leave it as it is for now and revisit at the next review.
James raised that he had read something about pension allowances in the press and was worried about over-contributing. I reassured him we would size the SIPP contributions appropriately and that the report would not commit to a figure that breached the limits.
There was a tangent about a property in France they had once considered buying; this is not being pursued and has no bearing on the advice.
To summarise the actions I noted: confirm Caroline's Meridian cash balance, and confirm the timing of the bridging-loan repayment.
Next steps: prepare the advice report covering the ISAs, the SIPPs, the joint GIAs, the offshore bond and the new joint account, and the investment of the completion proceeds.

=== internal_notes ===
# Internal notes: data sources

For whoever configures the report: what each source is, and how they relate.

## The sources

- **client_data_db.json**: a snapshot of the client's accounts taken from our custody systems on a
  schedule. It carries a `snapshot_date`, and every account carries its own `valuation_date`, the
  day that figure was last struck. It is the system of record for which accounts exist and who holds
  them.
- **meeting_notes.docx**: the adviser's file note from the most recent meeting. A free-form record
  of what was discussed and what the client decided.
- **report_request.docx**: the adviser's instruction for this particular report: which accounts to
  cover and the headline instruction.

## How they fit together

The db is where account structure and ownership live. The meeting note is where the conversation and
the decisions live. The two are produced at different times and for different reasons, so read the
date on a figure before you rely on it.

## Account data

Accounts are listed per holder. A jointly-held account is recorded under each holder it belongs to.
Not every field is populated for every account: a field may be blank where a figure was not captured
at snapshot time, and an account may carry a status.

## This client
The client holds accounts across more than one platform. He recently sold a business, and the proceeds arrive in more than one form and on more than one date; the meeting note has the detail.

# Investment Advice Report

## Introduction

Further to our recent discussions, we are writing to set out our advice in relation to your Stocks & Shares ISA, your jointly-held General Investment Account, your SIPP and your jointly-held Offshore Investment Bond. This advice is based on the information currently available to us.

This firm is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority.

## Background & Objectives

James and Caroline Whitmore are focused on achieving long-term growth while maintaining a balanced-to-moderate risk profile. With no immediate income requirements, they aim to build a tax-efficient investment base to replace income in three years, particularly in light of the recent sale of James's business and the associated emotional transition. Additionally, they have a commitment to repay a bridging loan, which will be a consideration in their financial planning.

The accounts covered by this report are as follows:

| Account | Owner | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| H4-ISA-J | James Whitmore | Stocks & Shares ISA | £85,000 |
| H4-GIA-HJ | Joint | General Investment Account | £255,000 (approx.) |
| B4-SIPP-J | James Whitmore | SIPP | £610,000 |
| B4-GIA-J | Joint | General Investment Account | £95,000 |
| M4-BOND-J | Joint | Offshore Investment Bond | £180,000 |
| H4-ISA-C | Caroline Whitmore | Stocks & Shares ISA | £82,000 |
| B4-SIPP-C | Caroline Whitmore | SIPP | £430,000 |

## Recommendations

We recommend the following:

To optimise your investment strategy for the new tax year, we recommend that you take the following actions. 

Firstly, utilise both of your ISA allowances. This will allow you to shelter more of your investments from tax, maximising your potential returns. You currently have £85,000 in your Stocks & Shares ISA (H4-ISA-J) and £82,000 in your other Stocks & Shares ISA (H4-ISA-C). 

Next, we advise making pension contributions into both of your SIPPs. You have £610,000 in your SIPP (B4-SIPP-J) and £430,000 in your other SIPP (B4-SIPP-C). Contributing to your pensions can provide significant tax advantages and help secure your financial future.

Additionally, consider adding to the Holloway joint General Investment Account (H4-GIA-HJ), which currently holds approximately £255,000. This will enhance your investment portfolio and provide further growth opportunities.

After these contributions, you should place the remaining balance into a new jointly-held investment account. This will allow for flexibility and diversification in your investment strategy.

Finally, we recommend disinvesting a portion of the Holloway joint GIA and rebalancing it. This will help to ensure that your investment allocation aligns with your risk tolerance and financial goals.

In total, you have £650,000 available to invest now, which comes from the completion payment. This amount, along with the proceeds from any disinvested accounts, will provide you with the necessary funds to implement these recommendations effectively.

## Tax Implications

The recommended disposal may give rise to a capital gains tax liability, which would be assessed against your annual exempt amount.

## Fees & Charges

The ongoing charges that apply are the platform charge levied by the platform and our ongoing advice charge. The initial charge on this recommendation is 0.5%. [FLAG: platform charge — ongoing platform charge to confirm] [FLAG: advice charge — ongoing advice charge to confirm]

## Next Steps

Before we finalise, there are some outstanding items to confirm:

- You also hold a Cash Account (M4-CASH-J, £30,000) that is not covered by this report. Please confirm whether it should be included or reviewed separately.
- You also hold a Cash Account (M4-CASH-C, balance to be confirmed) that is not covered by this report. Please confirm whether it should be included or reviewed separately.

## Conclusion

The value of investments can fall as well as rise and you may get back less than you invest. Past performance is not a guide to future returns.

If you are happy to proceed with our recommendations, please let us know and we will implement them for you.
